channel.title: Enthernet Blog
channel.description: Engineering in public: cloud, cybersecurity, automation, Linux, networking, containers, Kubernetes and research backed by real technical work.

item.title: Day 83: CI/CD Foundations
item.description: CI/CD turns source changes into a repeatable delivery path where validation, build, test and deployment decisions are explicit instead of depending on manual release memory.

item.title: Day 82: Kubernetes Production Deployment
item.description: The Kubernetes capstone connected scope, configuration, secrets, controllers, probes, networking, storage, ingress and Helm into one production-style deployment flow.

item.title: Day 81: Helm
item.description: Helm packages Kubernetes templates, defaults and metadata into configurable releases so environment differences do not require copy-paste manifests.

item.title: Day 80: Kubernetes Ingress
item.description: Ingress describes HTTP/HTTPS routing rules toward Services; an Ingress controller is the component that actually implements those rules.

item.title: Day 79: Kubernetes Persistent Storage
item.description: PersistentVolumes, PersistentVolumeClaims and StorageClasses separate application data from the lifecycle of individual Pods.

item.title: Day 78: Kubernetes Secrets
item.description: Kubernetes Secrets provide a dedicated object for sensitive configuration, but confidentiality still depends on access control, storage protection and application behavior.

item.title: Day 77: Kubernetes ConfigMaps
item.description: ConfigMaps separate non-sensitive application configuration from container images and can deliver values as environment variables or projected files.

item.title: Day 76: Kubernetes Namespaces
item.description: Namespaces scope namespaced Kubernetes objects so environments and teams can organize resources without making object names globally unique across the cluster.

item.title: Day 75: Kubernetes Services
item.description: A Service gives changing Pods a stable network endpoint and selects its backend endpoints through labels.

item.title: Day 74: Kubernetes Deployments
item.description: Deployments sit above ReplicaSets to manage stateless application rollouts declaratively, including replacement strategy and revision history.

item.title: Day 73: Kubernetes ReplicaSets
item.description: ReplicaSets continuously maintain a requested number of matching Pods and recreate missing replicas from a Pod template.

item.title: Day 72: Kubernetes Pods
item.description: A Pod is Kubernetes' smallest deployable compute object and groups one or more tightly coupled containers that share a network context and selected storage.

item.title: Day 71: Kubernetes Architecture
item.description: Kubernetes is a set of cooperating control-plane and node components that continuously reconcile declared state into running workloads.

item.title: Day 70: Multi-Container Deployment
item.description: The Docker capstone connected image build, private networking, persistent storage, health checks, secrets and runtime hardening into one small application system.

item.title: Day 69: Container Security
item.description: Container security reduces what a compromised application can do by removing unnecessary identity, filesystem, capability and host privileges.

item.title: Day 68: Dockerfiles
item.description: A Dockerfile is an ordered build recipe that turns source and dependencies into an image layer by layer.

item.title: Day 67: Docker Compose
item.description: Docker Compose describes a multi-container application, its network, storage, environment and startup relationships in one version-controlled file.

item.title: Day 66: Docker Networks
item.description: User-defined Docker networks let containers discover one another by names or aliases instead of coupling applications to replaceable container IP addresses.

item.title: Day 65: Docker Volumes
item.description: Volumes keep important state outside an individual container's writable layer so container replacement does not have to mean data loss.

item.title: Day 64: Docker Container Lifecycle
item.description: A container combines an image with runtime configuration, a primary process and a writable layer whose lifecycle differs from both the image and durable storage.
